title: Grade 12 — AP Lang, optimized for a 5
spine: Same CED skill categories as g11-ap-lang-4 at a higher bar, plus the skills that separate a 5 from a 4

scoreProfile.note: Design targets on the 3-row FRQ rubric, NOT official College Board cut scores. The 5 profile is the 4 profile plus sustained Row B ceilings and deliberately earned sophistication.
scoreProfile.rowB_evidenceCommentary: 4 of 4, sustained across all three FRQ types under time
scoreProfile.rowC_sophistication: earned on at least one FRQ per exam, by design not by accident

provenance.source: Derived 2026-09-15 from the g11 band plus the Row C / Row B-ceiling behaviors visible in officially scored high samples (studied lab-side; no College Board text reproduced)
provenance.note: The three added skills are what the scored-sample rationales consistently reward above the 4 line: complexity/tension, broader context, and vivid persuasive style — plus exam-scale stamina.

skills.title: Earn Row C deliberately: explore tensions, situate the broader context, sustain a vivid style
skills.rationale: Row C is scored as a property of the whole essay. It has to be taught as named, practicable moves — complexity between sources, implications beyond the prompt, controlled persuasive style — or it stays luck.

skills.title: Hold Evidence & Commentary at 4/4 across all three FRQ types under time
skills.rationale: The observable difference between most 4s and 5s is Row B consistency: specific, embedded evidence with commentary that never drops to paraphrase, on the weakest of the three essays, not the strongest.

skills.title: Run the whole exam: MCQ pacing plus three FRQs at 40 minutes each
skills.rationale: A 5 is a composite: strong MCQ over paired reading/writing questions plus three timed essays. Pacing and triage are trained skills with their own practice forms.
